name: Floor Sweeper
definition: A powered or manually propelled machine that uses one or more brushes to collect loose dry debris from a floor into an onboard hopper, often with suction and dust filtration on powered vacuum-sweeper designs.
includedScope: Manual, walk-behind and ride-on commercial floor sweepers
Indoor and outdoor sweeping within the limits stated by the manufacturer
excludedScope: Road sweepers and municipal street sweepers
Hazardous or combustible-dust collection unless the exact machine is approved for that duty
headline: Floor sweeper types, dust-control systems, performance metrics and buyer verification
description: This technical profile explains floor sweeper formats, debris flow, dust-control components, representative models and procurement checks while keeping manufacturer claims within their stated model and market scope.
metaDescription: Commercial floor sweeper guide covering sweeper types, dust control, specifications, components, representative models and procurement checks.
disclaimer: This is an independent category reference, not model-specific purchasing, safety, hazardous-dust or repair advice. Confirm the current manual, configuration, serial range, local compliance and service terms before use or procurement.

keyFacts.label: Primary soil type
keyFacts.value: Loose dry debris and dust within the machine's stated limits
keyFacts.evidence: Official manuals describe sweeping loose debris into a hopper and warn against prohibited materials or environments.
keyFacts.scope: Reviewed commercial models; wet, hot, hazardous and combustible materials require model-specific approval.

keyFacts.label: Collection path
keyFacts.value: Side brush to main brush to hopper, with dust filtration on vacuum sweepers
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturer documentation identifies side brushes, a cylindrical main brush, debris hopper and filtration or vacuum systems.
keyFacts.scope: Powered vacuum-sweeper designs represented by the reviewed sources; simple manual sweepers may omit active suction.

keyFacts.label: Operator formats
keyFacts.evidence: The reviewed official ranges explicitly classify machines across manual, walk-behind and ride-on formats.
keyFacts.scope: Commercial floor-sweeper terminology used by the reviewed manufacturers.

keyFacts.label: Dust control
keyFacts.value: Filter area, filter cleaning and sealing are configuration-specific
keyFacts.evidence: Official sources publish filter types or areas and describe filter-cleaning systems for named models.
keyFacts.scope: Named vacuum-sweeper configurations only; published values are not a hazardous-dust certification.

systemFlow.name: Edge gathering
systemFlow.role: Moves debris from edges and corners toward the main sweeping path.
systemFlow.evidence: Official manuals and product sources identify side brushes and their role at the machine edge.
systemFlow.scope: Models fitted with side brushes; quantity and adjustment vary.

systemFlow.name: Main sweeping
systemFlow.role: Lifts loose material into the collection path.
systemFlow.evidence: Reviewed documentation identifies the main brush and model-specific brush replacement or adjustment.
systemFlow.scope: Reviewed commercial sweepers; brush pattern and material are model-specific.

systemFlow.name: Debris collection
systemFlow.role: Stores collected debris for controlled emptying.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources state hopper capacities and emptying arrangements.
systemFlow.scope: Named configurations; usable capacity depends on debris density and loading.

systemFlow.name: Air separation
systemFlow.role: Controls airborne dust generated by sweeping.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturer sources describe vacuum, filtration and filter-cleaning systems.
systemFlow.scope: Vacuum sweepers only; performance boundaries and dust classes differ.

systemFlow.name: Traction and power
systemFlow.role: Propels powered machines and runs sweeping and dust-control systems.
systemFlow.evidence: Official product data identifies manual, battery and engine-driven configurations.

variants.name: Manual push sweeper
variants.limitations: No powered traction and typically less dust-control capability than powered vacuum sweepers.
variants.evidence: Kärcher and Hako classify reviewed compact machines as manual sweepers.
variants.scope: Named manual products, not every push sweeper.

variants.name: Powered walk-behind
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator walks behind a self-propelled or powered machine
variants.limitations: Achieved output depends on hopper stops, filter maintenance and route geometry.
variants.evidence: Official sources classify KM 75/40 W Bp and SW900 as walk-behind sweepers.

variants.name: Ride-on
variants.spaceConstraints: Larger envelope, turning circle and storage area
variants.limitations: Nominal productivity does not account for narrow aisles, dumping or transport.
variants.evidence: Tennant and Hako identify S16 and Sweepmaster 1200 RH as ride-on sweepers.

variants.name: Battery or engine powered
variants.taskScale: Power source selected for duty cycle and environment
variants.spaceConstraints: Charging, ventilation, fuel and emissions constraints vary
variants.limitations: Indoor suitability cannot be inferred from machine size alone.
variants.evidence: Official ranges disclose battery and combustion-engine variants.
variants.scope: Reviewed ranges; local indoor-emission rules and exact configurations must be checked.

performanceMetrics.name: Sweeping path
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Nominal width covered with the specified brush configuration
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: May be stated with or without side brushes
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Compare the same brush configuration and do not convert width directly into achieved productivity.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official specifications publish multiple sweeping widths based on brush fitment.

performanceMetrics.name: Theoretical area performance
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Nominal output under stated speed and width assumptions
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Turns, overlap, dumping, obstacles and filter service reduce achieved output.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official product data publishes area-performance values for named models.

performanceMetrics.name: Hopper capacity
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Volume, not debris mass or usable fill
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Debris density, hopper loading and emptying method affect duty cycle.

performanceMetrics.name: Filter area and cleaning
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: One input to dust-control maintenance and airflow stability
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Filter media, class and test method are not normalized across sources
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Filter area alone does not prove dust capture, hazardous-dust approval or whole-machine sealing.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources publish filter area or filter-cleaning features.

performanceMetrics.name: Gradeability and dimensions
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Supports route, ramp, doorway, lift and storage checks
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Operating and transport conditions may differ
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Use the fully configured machine envelope and manufacturer slope limits.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official specifications publish dimensions and gradeability for selected models.

applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturers position reviewed ride-on and walk-behind sweepers for industrial floors and production environments.
applicationFit.scope: Loose dry debris on surfaces within machine limits; no hazardous-area approval is implied.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Route length, aisle width, debris profile and dust risk should drive format selection.
applicationFit.assessment: A site trial should include the heaviest representative debris and tightest turn.
applicationFit.basis: Official industrial positioning and published machine envelopes.
applicationFit.limitations: Suitability for combustible, toxic, hot or wet material is not established.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Document debris types and obtain written manufacturer approval for the intended environment.

applicationFit.evidence: Official product materials include outdoor and car-park applications for selected sweepers.
applicationFit.scope: Weather, surface and gradient limits remain model-specific.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Surface joints, ramps, drainage and wind exposure can dominate performance.
applicationFit.assessment: Validate pickup and dust control on the actual surface under representative conditions.
applicationFit.basis: Manufacturer application statements and dimensional data.
applicationFit.limitations: No universal wet-weather or road-use suitability is established.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Trial ramps and rough sections and confirm storage and charging conditions.

applicationFit.evidence: Official sources position compact sweepers for commercial and public-facing areas.
applicationFit.scope: Dry debris and routes compatible with the named machines.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Noise, dust release, maneuverability and pedestrian separation require joint review.
applicationFit.assessment: Compact geometry may matter more than maximum width in occupied routes.
applicationFit.basis: Official application positioning and format descriptions.
applicationFit.limitations: Published sources do not establish suitability during public occupancy.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Run an occupied-hour risk assessment and representative route trial.

applicationFit.evidence: Ride-on sweepers are officially positioned for larger indoor and outdoor commercial areas.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Transit distance, dumping logistics and weather exposure should be included in productivity calculations.
applicationFit.assessment: Nominal sweeping width alone is insufficient for dispersed routes.
applicationFit.basis: Official large-area positioning and hopper specifications.
applicationFit.limitations: Road homologation and hazardous debris are outside this profile.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Time a full route including travel and hopper emptying.

componentStack.name: Main brush
componentStack.role: Lifts debris into the hopper path.
criticalChecks: Exact model and brush part number
componentStack.evidence: Manuals describe model-specific main-brush adjustment and replacement.

componentStack.name: Side brush
componentStack.role: Extends edge reach and feeds debris toward the main brush.
componentStack.evidence: Official documentation identifies optional or fitted side brushes.

componentStack.name: Hopper and dumping system
componentStack.role: Contains collected debris and supports emptying.
componentStack.evidence: Official sources document hopper capacity and manual or high-dump arrangements.

componentStack.name: Dust filter and vacuum path
componentStack.role: Controls airborne dust and maintains collection airflow.
componentStack.evidence: Official sources describe filtration and cleaning systems.
componentStack.scope: Filter family labels do not establish hazardous-dust performance or interchangeability.

componentStack.name: Power and traction system
componentStack.role: Drives propulsion, brushes and vacuum functions.
variants: Petrol or LPG on selected ranges
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturer specifications identify distinct power packages.

distinguishingSpecifications: 700 mm width with one side brush
representativeModels.evidence: Kärcher identifies KM 70/20 C as a compact manual sweeper and publishes the cited widths.
representativeModels.scope: Regional product page reviewed; confirm local product number.

distinguishingSpecifications: 750 mm working width with one side brush
representativeModels.evidence: Kärcher publishes the model format and cited configuration data.

distinguishingSpecifications: published sweeping paths by brush fitment
representativeModels.evidence: Tennant identifies S16 as a compact battery ride-on sweeper and publishes configuration-specific specifications.
representativeModels.scope: EMEA specification sheet; verify quoted options.

representativeModels.evidence: Nilfisk's brochure identifies SW900 and publishes the cited features.
representativeModels.scope: Brochure configurations; regional packs may differ.

distinguishingSpecifications: theoretical area performance stated by Hako
representativeModels.evidence: Hako identifies M600 as a walk-behind manual sweeper and publishes technical data.
Hako classifies 1200 RH as a ride-on vacuum sweeper and publishes variant data.
TASKI's information sheet identifies balimat 2300 and states the cited characteristics.
representativeModels.scope: Official information sheet; confirm regional availability.

procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating theoretical area performance as cleaned output
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources publish nominal or theoretical performance for named models.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Use a timed route including turns, transport, filter cleaning and dumping.
procurementDecisions.basis: Site losses are excluded from theoretical values.
procurementDecisions.limitations: WCB has not independently tested the models.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Specify a representative demonstration route and acceptance measure.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Record brush configuration, travel speed and debris load during the trial.

procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Using filter area as a standalone capture rating
procurementDecisions.evidence: Sources describe filters and cleaning systems but do not normalize whole-machine dust performance.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Filter media, seals, airflow and cleaning method must be evaluated together.
procurementDecisions.basis: Published attributes have different reporting boundaries.
procurementDecisions.limitations: This evidence does not establish combustible- or hazardous-dust approval.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Obtain written approval for the exact dust and environment and inspect seals during a trial.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm filter part number, class, seal set and disposal procedure.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Full configured envelope and dumping method
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Comparing body width without side brushes or hopper movement
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official specifications separate base dimensions, working width and hopper arrangements.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Doorways, turns, ramps, lifts and dump points require a route-level check.
procurementDecisions.basis: The operating envelope changes with brushes and dumping.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Published dimensions cannot represent every route obstruction.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Measure the minimum clearances and observe a full hopper-emptying cycle.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify operating mass, gradeability, dump height and overhead clearance.

procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Assuming all battery variants share runtime or charging infrastructure
procurementDecisions.evidence: Manufacturer sources identify battery-powered models and configuration-specific packs.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Match the complete battery and charger system to shift and facility power.
procurementDecisions.basis: Runtime depends on pack, settings, surface and duty cycle.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Request the quoted battery and charger part numbers plus a duty-cycle calculation.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm chemistry, voltage, input supply, ventilation and charging location.

engineeringChecks.reason: Hot, wet, toxic or combustible material may be prohibited or require purpose-designed equipment.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Document the material and obtain written manufacturer and safety approval.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manuals and OSHA guidance set material and combustible-dust boundaries.
engineeringChecks.scope: US OSHA guidance plus reviewed manufacturer instructions; local rules may add requirements.

engineeringChecks.reason: Dimensions, materials and interfaces are model-specific.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Verify machine model, serial range and exact service part numbers.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official manuals provide model-specific brush and filter service instructions.

engineeringChecks.reason: Machine envelope, turning and slope limits affect safe access.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Measure doors, turns, ramps, lifts and storage before quotation acceptance.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official specifications publish dimensions and operating limits for named machines.

engineeringChecks.reason: Voltage, chemistry, charger and facility input must match.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Record all quoted part numbers and verify site electrical provision.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official sources identify battery configurations for powered models.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-72:2021
standards.applicability: Particular safety requirements for floor treatment machines, including sweepers, for commercial use.
standards.evidence: IEC states the standard applies to powered ride-on and non-ride-on floor treatment machines for commercial indoor or outdoor use.
standards.scope: Confirm regional adoption, machine classification and exclusions for the exact product.

developments.title: IEC commercial floor-treatment safety edition published
developments.summary: IEC published the 2021 edition of IEC 60335-2-72 covering commercial floor treatment machines including sweepers.
developments.evidence: The IEC catalogue records edition 5.0 and publication date.
developments.scope: International base standard; regional implementation must be checked.
